items.title: Table 2 (m = 6), row 5 is shifted
items.detail: S(5, 6, 6), S(5, 6, 8), S(5, 6, 10) are 13/4, 17/4, 9/2; the paper prints 17/4, 9/2, 5, dropping 13/4. The whole row, never split, gives the same.

items.title: Table 7 (m = 2) breaks its own symmetry
items.detail: S(10, 2, 14) = −1/64 and S(14, 2, 10) = 1/64. The paper prints 1/64 and 1/16, which cannot both hold when S(2i, 2j, 2k) = −S(2k, 2j, 2i).

items.title: Decomposition conjecture: more exceptions
items.detail: S(k, m··, n) = S(k, m) + S(n) holds in 2662 of 2716 cases up to 14 outside the stated family, but fails for every S(1, 2j··, 2k) (49 cases; each equals the one-gap row S(1, 2j + 2k)) and for S(3, 4··, 2k), 2k ≥ 6 (5 cases).

items.title: The stated exceptions S(2j, 2j··, 2k), j odd, really do not decompose
items.detail: 28 of 28 fail, as the paper says.

items.title: Even-odd-even: "if i, k ≥ j" is too wide
items.detail: (j+1) + (k+i)·* fails in 97 of 188 cases; with i, k ≥ j + 2 it holds in 91/91.

items.title: Odd-even-odd formula as printed
items.detail: It assumes i ≥ k but then ranges over 2k+1 > 2i+1. Read off Tables 5 and 6 as −2^(d−j−1) (d = k − i ≤ j) and −(d − j) beyond, it holds in 196/196.

items.title: Even-even-even formulas: (j − k) should be (i − j)
items.detail: As printed they fail in 27/68 and 10/35 cases. With (i − j) + k·* for i < j < k and i − j + 1 for k = j they hold in 62/62 and 45/45.

items.title: Even-even-even conjectures: the shift is off by one
All other 742 table cells agree
items.detail: 749 cells in Tables 1–8 recomputed in 40 s; the paper's "1↑3*" is 1 + 3·↑ + *.

items.title: Odd-odd-odd = i + j + k; the odd-even-even conjecture
Splitting the row
items.detail: A golden-ratio weight shows no stone ever lands more than one square past the row, so parts whose reaches stay two squares apart are independent. Checked against the unsplit row on all 8192 rows of up to 13 squares: 0 differences.
